Hi Rachel / Laura,

Hope you’re both well. We’re in the middle of month-end at Lumenix and our cash conversion cycle is stretched this quarter — we’re asking a small set of vendors if they can temporarily extend payment terms while we close a receivables tranche.

Specifically: would Redwood consider moving our invoices to Net60 for the next two billing cycles, and increasing our credit cap to EUR 250,000 while we complete a scheduled financing draw? We can provide a purchase order and our VAT registration certificate.

Appreciate quick guidance so we can plan cash flows.

Hi Marc — thanks for flagging and for the heads-up. I ran this past finance and legal; here’s a practical compromise that we can execute quickly without an extended credit review: 

- Term: Redwood can approve Net45 for the next two billing cycles (instead of Net60).
- Payment schedule (proposed): 25% deposit on signature, 50% on go-live/milestone, remaining 25% due 45 days from invoice. I attached a one-page payment schedule for clarity (Redwood_payment_schedule_Lumenix_v1.xlsx).
- Credit cap: provisional increase to EUR 200,000 effective immediately; final bump to EUR 250,000 subject to a short credit check and receipt of PO + VAT cert.
- Early-pay incentive: 1% discount if invoice paid within 30 days for the first two invoices (we’re trying to help your cash position).
- VAT handling: please send your VAT registration certificate and confirm whether the reverse charge applies; we’ll reflect VAT on our invoices per EU rules.

Next steps I can action today: upload the proposed payment schedule to your HubSpot record, route the amended SOW for signature, and loop in Sean in finance to kick off a credit check.

If that sounds acceptable, please send the PO and VAT cert and I’ll get the paperwork moving.

Best,
